expectations.text: OUTPUT_DIR/plan.md exists and contains, in order, sections for: headline, approach summary, out of scope, plan steps, assumptions, test plan, risks and mitigations, open questions (names may vary slightly).
expectations.evidence: H2 order: Headline (l3), Approach summary (l10), Out of scope (l25), Plan (l34), Assumptions validated (l141), Project conventions (l181), Test plan (l196), Risks and mitigations (l234), Counterfactual (l242), Open questions (l254). check_run.py reports sections_in_order=false only because the H3 'Step 4. Service tests' (l112) matched 'test' first.

expectations.text: The headline is one to three sentences and states what is being built and the chosen approach; the approach summary is prose of three to ten sentences, not bullets.
expectations.evidence: The approach summary is fine at 10 prose sentences (4 in l12-15, 3 in l17-19, 3 in l21-23). The headline fails: 4 sentences in one paragraph (l5 'We derive...', l6 'No new event is written.', l7 'The `list` command prints...', l8 'The blocking decision...'), over the 1-3 limit.

expectations.text: The plan states a falsifier for the hypothesis: an observation that would prove the chosen shape wrong, separate from the individual assumptions.
expectations.evidence: l165 '**Falsifier.** A read-time derivation is the wrong shape if overdue must be a recorded fact.' Two triggering requirements are listed (l168-169), and 'The falsifier did not fire.' (l171).

expectations.text: Project conventions are cited with file:line from AGENTS.md or docs/guidelines.md: the test framework is unittest run by `make test`, lint is `make lint`, and no package manager or test runner from outside the repo (pytest, poetry, npm) is assumed.
expectations.evidence: unittest is cited from AGENTS.md (l183 '[`AGENTS.md:19-25`, ...] Python 3.11+, standard library only, `argparse`, `unittest`'). But `make lint` / `make test` are cited only from `Makefile:2-5` and `.github/workflows/ci.yml:11-12` (l184); step 7 (l137) runs them uncited. No AGENTS.md or docs/guidelines.md line backs them (AGENTS.md:22-23 and :88-89 are not cited for them). foreign_tools=[].

expectations.text: The plan cites the affected spec IDs by name: at least TKT-005 (due time by priority) and TKT-013 (listing order) or CLI-006 (list), and CLI-001 (the command list) as a spec that needs updating for the new subcommand.
expectations.evidence: TKT-005 (l58 in the TKT-014 draft), CLI-006 (l48), CLI-001 to update (l47 '"one of four subcommands" becomes "one of five"'). TKT-013 is not cited (check_run.py cites.TKT-013=false), but CLI-006 satisfies the 'or'.

expectations.text: The plan respects INV-001 and INV-002: overdue status is derived from the ticket's due time at read time and is never written to the event log as an edit or a new event, or if an event is proposed, the plan flags it as a spec change needing user approval.
expectations.evidence: Headline l6 'No new event is written.'; l19 'Nothing is appended to the log, so INV-001, INV-002, INV-005, and LOG-009 hold'; TKT-014 draft l59-60 'no event records that a ticket became overdue'; A4 (l148) log line count unchanged.

expectations.text: The plan reuses the existing due_at value on Ticket (or ticketdesk.sla.due_at) instead of recomputing SLA hours in the CLI or a new module.
expectations.evidence: Step 2 code l83 `now > self.due_at`; A1 (l145) quotes tickets.py:35-36; sweep l177 reuses `due_at()` through `Ticket.due_at`.

expectations.text: The plan names where `now` comes from for the overdue comparison (an injectable clock or time source consistent with EventStore.clock) and validates that assumption against the code.
expectations.evidence: Step 2 code l86-88 `now()` returns `self.store.clock()`. A3 (l147) validates with scratch/exp2_fake_clock.py (boundary results). l98 explains that INV-005 covers only event timestamps. Conventions l186 cite architecture.md:49-50 and :68-69.

expectations.text: Every load-bearing assumption in the assumptions section carries evidence: a file:line citation, a quoted doc passage, or a command output.
expectations.evidence: A1-A8 (l145-152) each carry evidence: file:line (tickets.py:35-36, store.py:26-27) or scratch output (exp1 padding, exp2 boundary, missing-log run, `invalid choice` exit 2, equal due times). Prototype output quoted l156-163.

expectations.text: The test plan names unittest test files under tests/ and at least these cases: a ticket exactly at its due time, a closed ticket past due (expected not overdue, or flagged as an open question), and the ordering of the overdue list.
expectations.evidence: tests/test_tickets.py (l198) and tests/test_cli.py (l208). Cases: 'at exactly its due time is not overdue' (l200), 'A closed ticket past its due time is not overdue, also when it closed late' (l202), due order not ID (l203), tie by ID (l204).

expectations.text: A counterfactual section maps each stated success criterion to a plan step and records Confirmed, Confirmed with gaps, or Unconfirmed.
expectations.evidence: '## Counterfactual' (l242-252): 'Verdict: confirmed with gaps', table maps 5 criteria to plan steps with failure evidence.

expectations.text: Open questions are listed explicitly (for example whether closed tickets count as overdue, the exit code when nothing is overdue) and none is silently answered in the plan steps without being named as an assumption.
expectations.evidence: 9 open questions (l258-266) with assumptions: boundary (Q3), closed (Q4), tie order (Q5), retroactive SLA (Q7). Exit 0 for an empty `overdue` comes from the existing CLI-008 (test l210), not invented.

expectations.text: Skim test: the first sentence of each paragraph in the headline and approach summary carries a claim a newcomer understands; no step numbers, shorthand, or teaser leads.
expectations.evidence: Leads: 'We derive "overdue" at read time from the replayed due time and the store's clock.' (l5); 'The service in `ticketdesk/tickets.py` gets the overdue rule, `Ticket.is_overdue(now)`.' (l12); 'The change leaves replay and all write paths alone.' (l17); 'Experiments confirmed that every replayed ticket carries `due_at` and that `OVERDUE` fits the 8-character state column.' (l21). All claims, no teaser.

expectations.text: `git status --porcelain` in OUTPUT_DIR/repo is empty: no code or doc was changed.

notes: 266 lines, the longest in this batch. It includes code sketches for step 2 and full proposed spec text.

Arithmetic in the tie-break test (P2, then P1 20 hours later) and the e2e due times (1700014400 vs 1700159200) is correct.
Headline lines l5-8 sit on separate source lines but render as one 4-sentence paragraph, which fails the 1-3 cap. The plan would work.
